# Goal

Make live-work attribution **per dispatch**, not per session turn, so a slot that
is genuinely prefilling a real local dispatch always carries its attribution
(AC1 of the parent) and the truthful-status contract is not weakened (AC2).

## Root cause (confirmed by log analysis, 2026-11-02)

`_decrement_local_active_queries` (normal end-of-stream teardown) writes
`local_dispatch_records[record_key]["active"] = False` +
`expires_at = now + lease_timeout` and logs `lease_renewed`. `record_key` is
`(endpoint, session_id)`, so the teardown of turn N clobbers the record already
re-acquired by turn N+1 of the same session whenever the teardown lands after
the admission (measured 0.3-0.6 s later, repeatedly, in production).
`_release_local_dispatch` has the mirror hazard: it `del`s the record
unconditionally, so a late abandonment release can delete a newer dispatch's
record entirely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A teardown (both the normal-end `_decrement_local_active_queries` path
  and the `_release_local_dispatch` abandonment/explicit-release path) affects
  **only the dispatch that owns it**: a later dispatch on the same session key
  keeps `active=True`, its `expires_at` and its attribution.
- AC2: A slot prefilling a real local dispatch never reports
  `capacity_hint=saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` / empty owner on
  fresh slot detail — it carries the live-work attribution.
- AC3: Retained-lease semantics unchanged: after the last teardown the record
  remains `active=False` with a future `expires_at` (`lease_renewed`), so slot
  retention and the post-stream cooldown behave exactly as before.
- AC4: `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` no longer falsely resets
  `local_active_queries` for this case (no `counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0
  (0 active dispatch records)` warning for a healthy back-to-back session), and
  the recovery path still zeroes a genuinely leaked counter.
- AC5: Truthful status unweakened (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM): a pool with live work
  still reads `saturated`; abandoned work still reads `abandoned_busy`;
  abandonment paths still emit `lease_released reason=<reason>`; the existing
  dispatch/lease/capacity test suites pass unchanged.
- AC6: The only observable behavioural deltas are the corrected in-flight
  counts; any change to admission/prefill-gate inputs is measured and recorded
  in a comment on this item (no cap or budget change).

## Minimal implementation

Two candidate mechanisms — the implementation picks one, guarded by the sibling
test item:

1. **Per-dispatch token** — the acquisition path already receives `request`;
   stamp a dispatch id on the record and on the request state, and have every
   teardown no-op when the id no longer matches (idempotent, also fixes the
   `_release_local_dispatch` delete hazard).
2. **Per-session live-dispatch refcount** — acquisition increments, teardown
   decrements, `active = count > 0`; ordering-insensitive. Must keep the
   `expires_at` safety net so a leaked increment cannot wedge the pool, and the
   recovery loop must reconcile the count.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (~L4180-4260),
  `_decrement_local_active_queries` (~L3062-3135), `_release_local_dispatch`
  (~L4293), `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` (~L6480-6656).
- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_race.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_generating_only_pool.py` — existing guards.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — consumes the record registry for the payload.
data.title: Scope dispatch teardown to its own dispatch (per-dispatch live-work attribution)

Close parent AC4 by recording, per poll, why each of the five "unattributable"
polls from the 2026-11-01 night happened — so the next measurement cycle inherits
an attributed class instead of a mystery.

## Finding (already established, needs recording + verification)

All five are the same class as the 65 others: the per-session dispatch-record
teardown race described on the parent. Each poll sits inside a prefill for a
local dispatch whose record `active` flag was cleared by the *previous* turn's
late teardown:

```text
2026-11-01 22:12:55,240 [local] POST (new turn) -> 22:12:55,282 lease_renewed (previous turn teardown)
           polls 22:12:57 / 22:12:58 / 22:13:00 read saturated + local_in_flight_requests=0
2026-11-01 23:02:16,450 [local] POST         -> 23:02:16,478 lease_renewed
           poll 23:02:37,677 saturated + in_flight=0; Stream started 23:02:37,680 (21.2 s prefill)
2026-11-01 23:03:3x  same shape
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each of the five polls (`22:12:58`, `22:13:00` x2, `23:02:37`,
  `23:03:32`) is recorded on this item with its log evidence (the `[local] POST`
  / `lease_renewed` / `Stream started` line timestamps that bracket it), and with
  the root cause named (cross-turn teardown race), so parent AC4 is satisfied by
  **attribution** rather than by "provably absent".

  is NOT attributed to LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (blocked) — that item remains a

  reason set cannot attribute, it is listed with its evidence and reported as an
  explicit, explained residual count (never silently dropped) — the discipline of
  LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR AC2 applied to this item's record.

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator reading the nightly usage report, I want a **Context size at fallback by percentile band** section rendered immediately after `## Local model usage by session`, so that I can see how much context the local model was carrying when sessions gave up on it and how much new (uncached) prompt work the final turn cost in each context band — instead of inferring it from the per-session table's `Context size at fallback` column.

Discovered from the proxy usage report (see `## Local model usage by session`, LP-0MVM93DE6009JGBU, and the fallback-reason table).

## Scope

Add one new report section, its derivation and its `--json` projection. No change to any existing section, column, JSON key or CSV.

### Section shape

Heading: `## Context size at fallback by percentile band`, placed **immediately after** `## Local model usage by session` (before `## Fallback reasons`).

Cohort: sessions with **at least one local turn** (the same cohort the `Local model usage by session` section uses — a local `Stream started` paired with a local `Stream finished`) **and** token evidence for their context at fallback (the same derivation that column already uses). Sessions with no token evidence are excluded from the banded figures and their count is stated in the section, never counted as 0.

Rows: decile bands of context size at fallback, `P0–P10`, `P10–P20`, … `P90–P100`, computed with the report's existing percentile convention (linear interpolation over the cohort, the convention the `Local model usage by session` percentile table already uses). The lowest band includes its lower bound; the highest includes the maximum.

Per band, one row carrying:

| Column | Definition |
|---|---|
| Band | `P0–P10` … `P90–P100` (plus the two context bounds in tokens for orientation) |
| Sessions | number of sessions in the band |
| Avg total context size | arithmetic mean of those sessions' context size at fallback (tokens) |
| Avg final-turn new tokens | arithmetic mean, over the same sessions, of the new (uncached) tokens on that session's **final turn** — the prompt's uncached remainder as recorded for that turn (`estimated_tokens` × (1 − `cached_ratio`) from the turn's routing/admission line, or the turn's measured `new_tokens` where present). Sessions whose final turn carries no token evidence are excluded from this column's average for that band and counted in the stated `n/a` tally — never imputed as 0. |

Then a **top-two fallback reasons per band** table: the two most common `Reason for remote fallback` values across the cohort (deterministic tie-break: higher count, then alphabetical), each shown as count **and** percentage **of that band's sessions**, with an explicit `other` remainder so each band's row is readable as shares of 100%. Reasons are categorical: counts and percentages only, no percentiles.

### Derivation rules (must not be reimplemented per surface)

- Reuse the existing `Local model usage by session` derivations (local-turn pairing, per-session fallback attribution, context-size-at-fallback derivation) rather than adding a second copy; the two sections must not be able to disagree about a session's context-at-fallback or fallback reason.
- The section is **omitted** (no heading, no zero-fill) when the cohort is empty (a window with no local turns, or a log directory with no logs), so the 05:00 cron exits 0 and an empty window still renders a clean report. In that case `--json` reports the new key's band list as empty and its cohort counts as 0.
- Purely additive: no LLM call, no network call, no interactive prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Section and placement.** `report.md` contains `## Context size at fallback by percentile band` immediately after the `## Local model usage by session` block and before `## Fallback reasons`; a test asserts the rendered section order (not just presence), and fails if the heading is missing or misordered.
2. **Cohort and exclusion accounting.** The section states the cohort size (sessions with ≥1 local turn), the number included in the banded figures (those with context-at-fallback evidence) and the number excluded for missing evidence; a test pins against a fixture where one eligible session has no token evidence (it must not appear as 0 and must be counted as excluded).
3. **Bands.** Exactly the ten decile bands are rendered for a populated cohort, each with session count, average total context size and average final-turn new tokens; band membership is verified by unit tests at the boundaries (a session exactly on a decile boundary lands in the higher band; the minimum lands in `P0–P10`; the maximum lands in `P90–P100`) and by a test that an empty band renders an explicit `-` rather than 0 or a fabricated mean.
4. **Averages.** A unit test asserts the band means against hand-computed figures on a small fixture, including that a session with no final-turn token evidence is excluded from that band's new-token average (mean of the remaining sessions) and counted in the `n/a` tally.
5. **Top-two reasons.** A test asserts the two reasons chosen (count ordering, alphabetical tie-break) and that their percentages are computed within each band (shares of that band's session count, plus an `other` remainder that makes each row sum to 100%).
6. **`--json` parity.** The same figures are exposed additively under a new key (proposed `context_at_fallback_by_percentile`, carrying the cohort counts, the per-band rows and the per-band top-two reason shares); a test asserts the JSON and the rendered table agree on every band figure, and an existing-key regression test asserts no pre-existing JSON key changed or disappeared.
7. **Not a silent zero.** For a window with no local turns, the section is absent from `report.md` and the JSON key is present with an empty band list and zero cohort counts — a test covers the empty window end to end.
8. **Docs.** `REFERENCE.md` documents the new section, its cohort definition, the percentile convention, the `n/a` exclusion rule and the new JSON key (outputs section), and `SKILL.md` gains a short paragraph describing the section; a test or doc-lint check keeps the documented JSON key name and the rendered heading in sync (same convention the other keys/headings follow).
9. **Determinism and gate.** Re-running the CLI over the same fixed window produces byte-identical section output modulo timestamp/archive lines; the changed-scope test gate passes (build → test → commit order).

## Assumptions (recorded, adjust if the operator prefers otherwise)

- "P10, P20, P30 etc." is interpreted as **disjoint decile bands** (`P0–P10`, `P10–P20`, …) rather than cumulative "≤ Pk" cohorts, because disjoint bands answer the operational question (does the dominant fallback reason shift as context grows?) and let the per-band reason shares read as 100% shares. If the operator wants cumulative bands, only the band-construction step changes; the columns, JSON shape and ACs stay.
- "Final turn" is the session's last turn **inside the analysis window** (the turn that determined its in-window context), with new tokens taken from that turn's recorded uncached remainder rather than recomputed from text.
- Percentiles use the report's existing linear-interpolation convention so this section and `Local model usage by session` agree.
data.title: Usage report: context size at fallback by percentile band (new section after local model usage)

## Goal

As an audit operator, I want `audit_runner.py issue <id>` to verify a work item whose delivered code lives in a **different repository** from its worklog-owning project, so a cross-repo item gets a real, evidence-based verdict instead of a mis-scoped one — or an explicit refusal naming the gap.

`discovered-from:LP-0MVVYQ1U3006GDWT` (found during that item's audit).

## Problem statement

Some work items are tracked in one project's worklog while their code lands in another
project's repository (recorded precedent: `LP-0MVVYQ1U3006GDWT`, `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4` —
item in the `llm-manager`/`LP` worklog, code in `~/projects/SorraAgents`).

The runner derives its **per-audit target root** from the worklog-owning project
(`_resolve_owning_project_root`: explicit `--worklog-dir` parent, else the prefix-to-sibling
scan — `audit_runner.py:~1803`). For a cross-repo item that root is the worklog owner
(`llm`), whose repository contains **none** of the delivered files. Consequences:

- the Phase 1 merge gate looks for the item's commits in the wrong repo (they are
  unresolvable there, so the gate fail-opens and records nothing useful);
- the code-quality scan scope resolves to an empty/wrong file set;
- the Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest lists the item's Key Files (which do not exist in the
  target repo) plus the wrong repo index, so a correct model judgement would mark every AC
  `unmet`/`partial`.

There is **no supported way** to point the git scope at the code repo while keeping `wl`
pointed at the worklog: passing `--worklog-dir` also sets the owning root to that worklog's
parent, and no target-root override flag/env exists. In practice such items are audited by
manual producer review (e.g. `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4`, "Approved by manual review") or by the
skill's Manual Fallback path with hand-gathered evidence.
Observed 2026-11-02 on `LP-0MVVYQ1U3006GDWT`: the audit had to be performed manually
against `~/projects/SorraAgents @ 3b9c44d20` (the canonical runner would have produced a
misleading `Ready to close: No` against the `llm` tree).

## Desired change

1. Let the runner resolve an **explicit code-repository root** for the git-derived content
   (merge gate, file-scope manifest, changed files, green-run evidence, code-quality scope,
   Phase 2 cwd) independently of the worklog store — e.g. a `--code-root DIR` flag /
   `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` env var, defaulting to today's behaviour (owning project). `wl` calls
   keep resolving to the worklog.
2. When no explicit code root is given and the item's resolved touched-file set is
   **entirely absent** from the owning repo while present in a sibling project, abort with a
   loud, actionable scope error naming the sibling candidate(s) rather than proceeding to a
   mis-scoped Phase 1/2 (fail closed like the existing `Audit scope error` paths).
3. Record the resolved code root in the persisted report (a `## Audit Scope` line) so a
   reader can tell which repository the evidence came from.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cross-repo item (worklog in project A, code in project B) audited with the new explicit
   code-root option resolves the merge gate, file-scope manifest, changed files, green-run
   evidence and code-quality scope against **B**, while every `wl` read/write still targets
   A's worklog (test asserts both, with two real temp git repos).
2. Without the explicit option, the same item fails closed with a scope error that names the
   sibling project(s) whose repository holds the item's touched files — before any Phase 1
   model call (test asserts zero `pi` invocations).
3. A same-repo item's behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged with and without the new option
   (regression test: identical manifest, HEAD attestation and verdict).
4. The persisted report records the resolved audit scope (code root + worklog) — verified by
   a report-format test.
5. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill; full suite green via the dev-push gate.

- Related guards to preserve: `_verify_launch_context` (undeterminable ownership aborts),

Discovered during LP-0MVTJXBKO00843I8 implementation (Quality Improvement - Refactoring epic). Reproducible at clean dev HEAD 1976307e with NO local changes.

Symptom: the finish gate's changed-scope selection for a change under .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/ emits a single pytest command combining the 12 skill test files with proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py. In that mixed invocation pytest picks up proxy/pytest.ini as the configfile and sets rootdir to <repo>/proxy, which changes module resolution for the skill tests: TestComputeGpuBusy then fails 3 tests with nodeids rendered as 'proxy::TestComputeGpuBusy::...' (compute_gpu_busy returns None because the test's mock patches a different module object than the one the test module bound).

Evidence: the exact 13-file selection fails (3 failed, 928 passed) while the same 13 files pass when given --rootdir=. (931 passed). Adding a repo-root pytest.ini (same markers) also makes the selection pass. The failure is order/rootdir dependent and pre-existing: proxy/pytest.ini wins rootdir determination because it is in an arg's ancestor chain while the repo root has no pytest config.

Impact: any change touching .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis cannot pass the changed-scope finish gate, and the error masquerades as unrelated test failures.

Suggested fix (choose one): (a) add a repo-root pytest.ini/pyproject [tool.pytest.ini_options] carrying the same markers so rootdir is stable; (b) make the test-selection emit skill tests and proxy tests as separate pytest invocations; (c) make proxy/pytest.ini not determine rootdir for out-of-tree args.

discovered-from:LP-0MVTJXBKO00843I8 (and related to test-failure LP-0MVYNLWWL009R49W).

The order-dependent full-suite defect fixed by c70b5f6c (consumer-side defensive pop in scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py) was treated at the consumer. The root cause is still live: aggregation.compaction_impact()'s best-effort 'from proxy.provider import effective_per_slot_threshold' resolves 'import proxy' against <repo>/proxy (a PEP 420 namespace dir with no __init__.py) and, when it fails, leaves a broken/None entry in sys.modules['proxy'] that poisons any later same-process import of the real package (proxy/proxy/).

A validated hardening exists (authored during LP-0MVWEBY3Y007EZNZ, retained in the worktree diff history): after the failed import, pop the stale 'proxy' entry (and any 'proxy.*' submodules) so the next importer resolves the real package — plus a matching regression test that asserts the reference tool survives a poisoned cache.

NOT landed because changing aggregation.py widens the changed-scope selection into the broken mixed rootdir selection tracked as LP-0MVZ8FSAS009MD25. Land this once that selection defect is fixed.

Acceptance criteria:
1. aggregation.compaction_impact() drops a stale sys.modules['proxy'] entry (None residue or PEP 420 namespace package) after its best-effort proxy provider import fails, without touching a genuinely imported __init__.py-backed proxy package.
2. A regression test proves a poisoned sys.modules['proxy'] does not break a subsequent same-process import of proxy.measured_cache_abort.
3. Full suite and the changed-scope gate are green.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator of the LLM proxy, I want a measured verdict on whether keeping session prompt prefixes resident actually moves more work onto the local model, so the residency fixes are credited (or rolled back) on numbers rather than intent.

**Primary metric: tokens processed locally. Secondary metric: GPU busy %.**

## Gating preconditions (do not start before all hold)

1. The residency-retention work has shipped **and been deployed** to the live proxy (parent: `Keep local prompt prefixes resident: tenancy hold, tenant bound, cache headroom, save/restore reliability`).
2. The deployed process is confirmed to be running the new configuration — the effective values are read back from the startup log / `.worklog` config dump, **not** assumed from the config file.
3. The measurement window starts at least 24 h after the deploy, so rollout churn and warm-up are outside the window.
4. No other local-routing change (slot geometry, admission pricing, ctx-size) lands inside the window. If one does, the window is restarted and the reason recorded.

## Baseline (nightly report, window 2026-11-01 11:09:07 → 2026-11-02 11:09:07)

Same 24 h length, same CLI, same log directory — the comparison must be like-for-like. Baseline report: `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` (retained at `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-02_3/`).

| Metric | Role | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| **Tokens processed locally** (local `Qwen3` input + output from `Stream finished tokens=`) | **primary** | **37,954,924** (input 37,517,955 / output 436,969) |
| **GPU busy — power-based (hardware)** | **secondary** | **66.4%** (57,400 s of 86,400 s) |
| Local busy (log-derived, dispatch → finish) | support | 41.7% (36,029 s) |
| Local turns (answered / unanswered) | support | 1,811 / 3 (local turn share 16.1%) |
| Post-acceptance evictions | support | 254 (prefill_deadline 126, measured_cache_deficit 99, watchdog 21, idle 6, lease 2) |
| Within-budget ETA/deadline refusals | support | 1,865 |
| Wasted prefill tokens / deadline cancellations | support | 796,993 / 128 |
| `resident_prefix_insufficient` skips | support | 7,912 |
| Residency decisions with a **measured** ratio | **validity** | 93 of 14,043 (0.7%) |
| Requests / sessions / total tokens (context for normalisation) | confound | 30,230 / 569 / 968,358,454 |

## Acceptance criteria

1. **A like-for-like 24 h post-deploy report exists** at a recorded path, produced by the same CLI over the same log directory with the same 24 h window length, and both the baseline and post-deploy report paths are recorded in the closing comment (plus the archive directory, since each run archives the previous outputs).
2. **Primary metric reported with a verdict.** Local tokens processed are compared with the 37,954,924 baseline as an absolute and a percentage change. Verdict: **met** at ≥ **+15%**, **partially met** at +5% to +15%, **not met** below +5%, with the measured figure and the threshold stated together. Prompt (input) and completion (output) tokens are reported separately, because a residency win shows up mostly as **input** tokens (more context served locally per turn), not output.
3. **Secondary metric reported with a verdict.** GPU busy % (power-based, `avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[24h])`) is compared with the 66.4% baseline; verdict **met** at ≥ **+5 percentage points**, and the log-derived local busy figure is reported beside it (the hardware figure counts non-proxy GPU work, so a rise must be corroborated by log-derived local busy).
4. **Validity gate is explicit.** The window is declared invalid and re-run if any of these fail, each named in the report: (a) residency decisions carry measured ratios materially above the 0.7% baseline (otherwise the fix was not observably live); (b) no local-routing config change inside the window; (c) `Streams without usage` for local streams stays comparable (11 baseline) so a token-total drop cannot be mistaken for a residency effect; (d) the window contains no multi-hour proxy outage.
5. **Confound normalisation.** Because local tokens are demand-driven, the report also states tokens-per-request, local turn share and local turns, and flags any request-volume change beyond ±20% of the 30,230 baseline. The verdict names which metric moved (more demand vs more local share vs better residency) so a volume swing cannot be reported as a residency win.
6. **Supporting metrics reported, not gated.** Evictions (254), within-budget refusals (1,865), wasted prefill tokens (796,993) and `resident_prefix_insufficient` skips (7,912) are compared and expected to fall; any rise is called out as a regression with a follow-up work item.
7. **Verdict recorded.** The verdict, the two headline figures with thresholds, the validity gate result and any follow-up items are recorded as a comment on this item; the work-item description is updated with the final comparison table so the result is readable without opening the report.
8. **No ad-hoc test invocation.** Any test-suite run goes through the test skill, per the shared test-execution policy.

## Notes

- The report's own **GPU busy** row is hardware activity (any GPU draw ≥ 90 W) and is *not* local model utilisation; that is why AC3 requires the log-derived local busy figure to corroborate it and why the primary metric is tokens processed locally, not GPU busy.
- If the primary metric is met but the residency measurement coverage (AC4a) is still at the baseline 0.7%, the result is a correlation, not a mechanism: record it as such and keep the `/slots` freshness dependency visible.
- Token totals depend on `tokens=` on `Stream finished` lines (LP-0MVMBM6N400541EH); a change in the count of local streams without usage invalidates a straight total comparison and must be stated.
## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — the deterministic report CLI; run over the same log dir and 24 h window for both baseline and post-deploy runs (records the report path + archive dir in the closing comment).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` — power-based GPU busy (`avg_over_time(gpu:computing:bool[24h])`); the secondary metric.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — local token totals, local busy, residency-decision and supporting-metric aggregation.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — parses `Stream finished tokens=` (LP-0MVMBM6N400541EH) and `routing_resident_prefix` decision lines; source of token totals and the measured-ratio validity check.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — effective local-routing knobs (residency, slot geometry, admission pricing, ctx-size) to confirm no config change landed inside the window.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` + `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-02_3/` — baseline artifact and location of the new post-deploy report; each run archives the previous outputs.

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVSN0OHG0024LH4** – Proxy usage report: hardware power-based GPU busy time (15s sampling) (completed)
- **LP-0MVUIM7A50053EFN** – Labelling + tests: log-derived local_busy is the decision figure (completed)
- **LP-0MQJGW3LO000H14M** – Test: Prometheus token-rate metric verification (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 24h, absolute, ac3, activity, actually (+230 more)
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 24h, absolute, ac3, acceptance, activity (+224 more)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 24h, absolute, ac3, acceptance, activity (+221 more)

## Goal

Compute discrimination metrics for candidate `gpu_metrics` activity fields against an explicit pass/fail bar, so a verdict rests on reproducible numbers rather than eyeballing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/lib/gpu_metrics_verdict.py` exports `compute_verdict(samples)` returning per-field statistics: idle-band mean (< 60 W), compute-band mean (>= 90 W), separation in percentage points, Pearson r against package power, and idle-band false-busy share (samples >= 90 % activity while power < 60 W), plus the per-band sample counts.
- [ ] A field passes only if separation >= 30 pp **and** r >= 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy <= 10 %; the module returns an explicit pass/fail decision per field, never a bare number.
- [ ] `tests/test_gpu_metrics_verdict.py` drives synthetic saturated (all 100 %), graded (low in idle, high in compute), flat-low, and noisy series, asserting the exact pass/fail decision and the computed statistics for each.
- [ ] Boundary cases are covered: power exactly 60 W and exactly 90 W (band assignment), activity exactly 90 % (false-busy threshold), and separation exactly 30 pp / r exactly 0.6 (pass edges).
- [ ] A capture covering only one band reports insufficient data rather than a misleading verdict.

## Constraints

- Pure Python stdlib only (implement Pearson r directly; no numpy dependency).
- Input is a list of sample dicts carrying at least `power_watts` and each candidate activity field, so the module has no knowledge of sysfs or file formats.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/lib/gpu_metrics_verdict.py` - New. Band statistics, Pearson r, false-busy share, the pass/fail bar and its constants.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_verdict.py` - New. Synthetic-series arithmetic, boundaries, one-sided captures.

## Goal

Decode the 264-byte `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob from `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` into named fields, validating the header so a kernel/firmware change fails closed instead of silently misparsing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/lib/gpu_metrics_decoder.py` decodes the blob into a dict of named fields using a pinned v3.0 field table transcribed from `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`) under `#pragma pack(4)`, with the cited source recorded in a docstring/comment.
- [ ] The header is validated: `structure_size` must equal the layout size (264 B, 260 B of fields + 4 B tail padding) and `format_revision` must equal 3; any mismatch raises a clear error naming the observed and expected values.
- [ ] Truncated or oversized buffers are rejected with a clear error rather than misparsed or partially decoded.
- [ ] `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` is a committed real 264-byte capture from this host, and a test asserts the decoded values against the numbers observed at intake (e.g. `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW, `average_gfxclk_frequency` in 2 711-2 900 MHz).
- [ ] A decode of the committed fixture cross-checks `average_socket_power` against the recorded hwmon `power1_average` value to within 1 %.
- [ ] `tests/test_gpu_metrics_decoder.py` covers the real fixture, a truncated buffer, an unknown `format_revision`, an unknown `structure_size`, and a zero-length file.

## Constraints

- Layout must be pinned in-repo; the struct is not shipped in this host's installed `linux-headers`.
- No root, no ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`: a single 264-byte world-readable sysfs read.
- Fail closed on any revision or size the code does not know.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/lib/gpu_metrics_decoder.py` - New. Pinned v3.0 field table, `#pragma pack(4)` layout, header validation, named-field decode.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_decoder.py` - New. Fixture round-trip plus every rejection path.
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` - New. One committed real capture.

## Goal

When `priority=high` (never queues), `wait_budget_seconds()` returns 0 and `evaluate_admission()` returns inert `no_budget` **before** the prefill-deadline and safety-budget bounds run (proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py). High-priority local dispatches are therefore never priced and never bounded: the 120 s `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` backstop is the only thing that stops them, and it fires after wasting the prefill.

Measured (LP-0MVZ5WV6W008UO5F AC1, window 2026-11-01 11:09 to 2026-11-02 11:09): **43 of 126** `prefill_deadline` evictions were `priority=high` with no `local_admission_guard` line at the dispatch instant - including **6 of the 7 evictions whose stamped ETA was already above the 120 s deadline (278.8-325.9 s)**. 6 in a single session (`herdr-1793573044-1512209-23699`) that repeatedly re-admitted a 20k+ new-token cold prompt. 257,778 priced new tokens discarded. All 43 were inside the 25k cold-prefill budget.

Key root cause in the guard: the cold-prefill budget check still binds for high priority, but the deadline and deadline-relative bounds are skipped because they sit after the `budget <= 0` early-return.

## Decision (producer, 2026-11-02)

**High-priority dispatches are bound in the same way as anything else.** `high` means "never queue", not "unbounded": the deadline (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`) and the deadline-relative safety budget (`local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction`) apply to `high` exactly as to `low`/`medium`. Only the *queue-wait* comparison is inapplicable (there is no queue to wait in). Recorded on this item (comment LP-C0MVZFW3PE006RXCD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For every `priority=high` local dispatch the guard skips only the queue-wait comparison (no queue exists) and still evaluates the prefill-deadline and safety-budget bounds against the priced ETA, refusing exactly as it does for `low`/`medium` — a prompt that fits both bounds still admits unchanged, and the decision is logged (`decision=admit` with reason `within_budget`, or `decision=reject` with the bound's own reason) instead of being silently inert.
2. No behaviour change for budgeted (low/medium) priorities - their admission path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
3. The decision is documented (config comment + routing.md + the proxy-usage-analysis attribution rule) and a post-change 24 h window shows the `high_priority_inert` attribution count at 0 via `attribute_prefill_deadline.py`, with local share not regressing below the rung-enabled baseline.
4. Full project test suite passes via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` - `wait_budget_seconds()` / `evaluate_admission()` bound ordering
- `proxy/config.yaml` - `local_admission_guard_*`, `local_prefill_deadline_seconds`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` - deadline interaction tests
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/attribute_prefill_deadline.py` - attribution CLI (LP-0MVZ5WV6W008UO5F)

## Triage

- Reproduced by: `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/attribute_prefill_deadline.py --start 2026-11-01 11:09:07 --until 2026-11-02 11:09:07` -> `high_priority_inert: 43`
- Discovered via: discovered-from:LP-0MVZ5WV6W008UO5F

## Goal

An admission-guard decision is logged only when it is **active** (within_budget, eta_exceeds_budget, deadline/safety-budget refusals, prefill_budget_exceeded). Inert decisions - `no_budget`, `insufficient_samples` (uncalibrated bucket), `policy_off` - log nothing (proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py `record_guard_decision`). The dispatch record still carries a priced ETA (the inert decision could price the prompt, e.g. `insufficient_samples`), but the admit is invisible in the log.

Measured (LP-0MVZ5WV6W008UO5F AC1): **47 of 126** `prefill_deadline` evictions had **no** `local_admission_guard` line at the dispatch instant, were not `priority=high`, and were not admitted by an override - they are un-attributable from the log alone (the 7th over-deadline case, a `priority=medium` event with a stamped ETA of 170.3 s at 2026-11-02 11:01:23, is in this class). 439,307 priced new tokens discarded. The current window shows these dispatches re-admitting the same uncached ~78k prompt shape that is then cancelled at the deadline - consistent with an uncalibrated `(model, context-bucket)` window that never accumulates served samples because the bucket's dispatches are all evicted (a self-reinforcing trap).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The inert path admitting each of these dispatches is established from the log (either by logging inert admits at debug level, or by emitting a `reason=inert_admit samples=N` line on the `local_admission_guard` line without changing the verdict) with a measured 24 h count.
2. Attribution is possible without raw-log archaeology: the report CLI (`attribute_prefill_deadline.py`) distinguishes `inert_unlogged` by inert reason when the evidence permits.
3. Documentation (SKILL.md triage rule) tells the operator how to read the class and what to fix.
4. Full project test suite passes via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` - `record_guard_decision` / `AdmissionDecision.active`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` - `_prefill_admission_guard` (inert returns before logging)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/attribute_prefill_deadline.py` - attribution CLI (LP-0MVZ5WV6W008UO5F)

## Goal

A session that re-sends a byte-identical conversation and receives a deterministic local HTTP 400 must get a typed client error immediately (so the agent can compact and retry), must not consume global chain-hold cycles, and must be backed off per prompt fingerprint instead of retried every couple of minutes forever.

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- herdr-1793690708-3599162-11470 looped "cache_invalidation: full re-process required - no_new_messages (delta_message_count=0)" then "Deterministic local HTTP 400 ... consecutive=2 threshold=2" 8 times between 08:45:05 and at least 09:15:46.
- herdr-1793690345-3593722-18975 did the same once (08:46:17).
- Each 400 fired a global "All providers exhausted ... Chain exhausted ... holding 120s/300s", which starved every other session -- including the audit that was failing to get a slot.

## Decision recorded on this item

Neiher an immediate terminal close of the session nor a single fixed 90-minute delay. The error is deterministic for a given history but the client can self-heal (compaction/truncation), so: fail fast with a typed 4xx, back off per fingerprint (1 -> 5 -> 15 min, capped), never touch chain hold, and only escalate to a terminal per-session error after N byte-identical resends within the backoff window.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A deterministic local 400 returns immediately with a machine-readable code (deterministic_client_error, reason=identical_history) and a short Retry-After; no chain_hold_cycle is consumed and no other session's routing is affected.
- AC2: Repeat requests with the same prompt fingerprint are backed off on an exponential schedule (1 -> 5 -> 15 min cap); the backoff resets on any successful stream for that session or on a changed history.
- AC3: After N byte-identical resends the session receives an explicit terminal error naming the cause and pointing at history size/shape, instead of hanging.
- AC4: Tests cover: single 400 does not enter chain hold; repeat 400s respect backoff; a changed history clears the backoff; a successful stream clears the backoff.
- AC5: The proxy-usage-analysis taxonomy reports deterministic_client_error separately from provider exhaustion.
data.title: Typed deterministic client error and fingerprint circuit breaker for wedged sessions

## Goal

Serialise audit runs at the resource they actually contend for -- the single local llama-server -- rather than per host or per repository, so that N projects cannot launch N concurrent audits against one GPU.

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03 08:30-09:10)

- Five audits plus one plan run overlapped: RISE-0MVZEOVQG0075XSU, RISE-0MVXW2HRT000GO5E, MS-0MVZLKEU5000Q7SQ, WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD, AH-0MVX2DKC8001RRM4, and /skill:plan WL-0MVHP5S01006GDDV.
- Load was 592,452 prompt tokens and 4,345 decoded tokens across 30 streams in 40 minutes -- almost pure prefill on one GPU.
- ContextHub already has a single-active-audit guard (downtime-worker.dispatch.ts) with reason audit-in-flight / audit-host-saturated, but: the per-worklog scope serialises within one repo (four repos here), and the host-wide marker is a file at ~/.herdr/downtime/active-audit documented in machine-coordination.ts as "single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) is out of scope".
- The proxy sees two agent hosts: client_ip 192.168.0.191 (4,673 requests) and 192.168.0.199 (855) plus loopback. One GPU, two hosts, each enforcing one audit per host.
- The audit skill's own audit-batch queue is per-project, so it does not serialise across projects either.

## Scope note

Spans two repositories: this repo (audit skill / proxy) and ContextHub (herdr downtime worker). Plan to create a ContextHub child item for the dispatcher side, and keep this item for the audit-skill and proxy-side admission.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A proxy-side audit admission token exists (or an equivalent shared-resource gate) such that at most one audit-tier session holds it across all client hosts; a second audit waits rather than competing.
- AC2: The audit-batch queue is cross-project: an audit dispatched for repo A and one for repo B are serialised by the same queue, and the batch drain reports items_included across projects.
- AC3: The dispatcher's capacity decision uses the lease-derived availability signal (see the sibling lease-occupancy item), not raw version counts, and the mismatch between dispatcher admission and proxy refusal is impossible.
- AC4: Documented and tested: two concurrent audit dispatches from two different hosts (simulated distinct client identities) result in one running and one waiting, with a log line per decision.
- AC5: ContextHub child item records the single-machine limitation of ~/.herdr/downtime and the chosen cross-machine mechanism.
data.title: Serialise audits at the shared local resource, not per host or per repo

## Goal

Make the pre-dispatch prefill price reflect measured reality, and make in-flight prefill progress observable so the dispatch lease is extended on real progress and a runaway prefill is aborted early rather than discovered at 53-72 s.

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- routing_check at 08:41:54: estimated_tokens=18516 new_tokens=173 cached_ratio=0.99 cache_state=warm. llama-server then prefilled 13,002 new tokens; measured_cache_abort recorded measured_new_tokens=12936 priced_new_tokens=173 deficit_ratio=0.659. The turn took 53.2 s to first byte.
- Repeated at 08:43:14/08:44:26: priced_new_tokens=4695 measured_new_tokens=9264 deficit_ratio=0.285, turn took 72.0 s to first byte.
- The append that broke the estimator was a single tool-role message of 51,945 bytes at 08:41:54 (a full SKILL.md pasted into history); the in-memory residency ratio believed the 6.6k prefix was still resident when llama had 6,622 tokens and the new prompt was 19,628.
- prefill_progress_unobservable fired three times for this session (08:41:50, 08:42:59, 08:44:04); the lease was extended blind every 10 s (lease_extended_during_prefill progress=None alive=False). Eviction events show slot_id=unknown llama_task_id=unknown, so the proxy cannot map its request onto a llama task even though llama-server's /slots is being polled.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: When the appended content exceeds a configurable size threshold, the pre-dispatch price forces a full-prefill estimate (cached_ratio 0) rather than trusting the in-memory residency ratio; test asserts the 51,945-byte tool-append case is priced as a full prefill.
- AC2: post-measurement divergence (deficit_ratio above threshold) feeds back into the session's pricing/residency model so the next turn does not repeat the same under-estimate. Test asserts the second turn is priced from the corrected model.
- AC3: Each dispatched local request is associated with its llama task id (or slot id) so progress is observable; prefill_progress_unobservable is no longer emitted for the normal path, and lease extension uses measured progress.
- AC4: A prefill that exceeds its ETA bound by a configured factor is aborted early with a diagnosable event rather than after the full wait.
- AC5: A replay test using the recorded request sequence from ~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/herdr-1793695298-3654733-20033 reproduces the pricing correction.
data.title: Price prefill from measurement and map requests to llama slot/task ids

## Goal

Batch work (audit and plan children) must identify itself so priority routing can protect interactive sessions; today every request arrives with no priority header and is treated as low priority.

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- Every routing decision in the window logged priority_decision priority=low header=(none) -- for interactive panes, audit subprocesses and plan children alike. Priority routing therefore had no signal to act on while five audits plus a plan run competed for one GPU.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The audit skill's runner and the plan/intake dispatch paths send an explicit priority header (batch) on every pi/model call, carried through the proxy's priority_decision log.
- AC2: Interactive (herdr pane) sessions do not set the batch header, and priority routing demonstrably prefers them under contention (test with two concurrent sessions).
- AC3: The header is documented in the proxy config docs and validated (unknown/invalid values fall back to the default rather than erroring).
data.title: Batch work must send a priority header so interactive sessions are protected

## Goal

Right-size the llama-server prompt cache and checkpoint budget so that the local model does not spend most of its time re-prefilling prefixes it has already processed.

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- llama-server prompt cache was 39,829 MiB of a 40,960 MiB limit with 26 prompts, several holding the full 32 checkpoints at 62.8 MiB each (e.g. 2,925 MiB, 2,998 MiB, 2,494 MiB per prompt). Cache updates took 234 ms and prompt_save wrote 439 MiB of state per task switch.
- Over 08:30-09:10 the box processed 592,452 prompt tokens for 4,345 decoded tokens.
- Observed prefill rates in the log: median 122 tok/s overall, 143-303 tok/s for the large re-prefills, 598 tok/s best case. Note the documented caveat that "forcing full prompt re-processing" is expected for this hybrid architecture -- the concern here is volume, not the message.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A measurement (using the existing slot/eviction logging) quantifies how much re-prefill is caused by cache eviction versus genuinely new tokens over a representative window.
- AC2: A recommended cache-ram and ctx-checkpoints configuration is produced with the measured trade-off stated (killed prompts, checkpoint resume value, MiB per prompt), and applied to models.ini with a comment recording the measurement and its date.
- AC3: Post-change measurement shows a documented improvement in the prompt-token to decoded-token ratio, or a recorded decision that the current sizing is correct with the evidence.
data.title: Right-size the llama-server prompt cache and checkpoint budget

## Goal

Decide deliberately whether the second local slot is capacity or waste, and make the system use it (or stop advertising it as available).

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- llama-server runs 2 slots (total_slots=2, n_ctx 131072 each) and session_slot_pool_size is 2, but from task 191941 (08:43) through roughly task 193700 every launch was slot id 0 -- about 1,200 consecutive tasks on one slot. Slot 1 reappeared at task 193715 only once two requests genuinely overlapped.
- Normal agent traffic is not slot-pinned: id_slot is set only by compaction_summarizer.py; mainline requests let llama-server choose, and it picks by prompt-prefix similarity (1,040 selected slot by LCP similarity versus 39 by LRU). With the proxy granting one dispatch lease at a time there is never a second in-flight request, so slot 0 always wins and slot 1 is never launched.
- The signals disagree: available_slots reported 0 (lease-derived) at 08:50:47 while llama had a free slot, and 2 at 08:49:31 while the lease gate denied a dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Root cause recorded with supporting log evidence for why slot 1 goes unused in serialised operation, including the LCP-similarity versus LRU selection behaviour.
- AC2: A decision is recorded: either (a) enable deliberate two-session concurrency with cache-aware placement (so a second session is routed to a slot whose prefix it can reuse, avoiding a second full prefill), or (b) treat the local model as a single-slot resource for admission purposes and stop counting the idle slot as capacity in status and in client capacity decisions.
- AC3: The chosen option is implemented behind tests: a two-concurrent-session test asserts either two slots are used with reused prefixes, or the second request waits with an accurate capacity signal.
- AC4: Docs (models.ini slot commentary and docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md) are updated to match the decision.
data.title: Decide deliberately whether the second local slot is capacity or waste

data.description:
## Goal

**As an** operator, **I want** a measured verdict on the two chain/routing fixes shipped on 2026-11-03, **so that** "it is fixed" is a claim backed by a like-for-like before/after comparison against the configuration's own scheduled windows — not by the absence of complaints.

**Earliest implementation time: 2026-11-04 04:00 UTC.** That is the end of the first remote-closed window (`01:00-04:00` UTC) that completes after the 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC restart, so it is the first instant with (a) ≥13.5 h of post-fix log and (b) a full scheduled-gap sample. See **Timing** for why 2026-11-04 10:00 UTC is the *preferred* like-for-like point.

discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK, discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5.

## What is deployed

| Item | Commit | What it should change |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK — fail fast on a provably dead chain | `7892d22d` | no chain hold when every provider is deterministically skipped or terminally refused; earliest-reset `Retry-After`; a `remote-ok` request is never bounced onto a chain with no capacity |
| LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 — diagnosable lease occupancy | `763ed61f` | `local_dispatch_denied` carries the full occupancy evidence; `local_occupancy_divergence` names contradictions; stale records cannot block |

Deployed by restart **2026-11-03 14:25:09–14:25:10 UTC** (proxy pid 158427; `llama-server` and TTS relaunched and all three healthy). **The post-fix measurement window starts at 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC** (log rotation line `14:25:10,847 - INFO - Rotated previous proxy log`). Anything before that line is pre-fix.

## Timing: when the fix can actually fire

`model=code` has 7 providers; the gates that create a *provably dead* chain are the `available_times` windows:

| Provider | `available_times` (UTC) | Closed |
|---|---|---|
| `local-qwen3` | unrestricted | — |
| `munitoai-free` | unrestricted | gated only by usage-limit reset / quota |
| `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go-3` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `deepseek-flash` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `munitoai` | `10:00-23:00` | **23:00–10:00** |

So the chain is *window*-dead only in **01:00–04:00** and **06:00–10:00** UTC, and it is only *provably* dead when `munitoai-free` is also out (usage-limit reset / quota) — which is exactly the 2026-11-03 08:41 shape. `munitoai-free`'s recorded reset was `2026-11-04T00:02Z`, so **the 01:00–04:00 gap on 2026-11-04 may legitimately have a live provider and therefore no trigger**; that is correct behaviour, not evidence of anything.

Therefore:

- **earliest defensible evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **04:00 UTC** (first complete post-fix gap);
- **preferred like-for-like evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **10:00 UTC**, i.e. the end of the `06:00–10:00` gap — the same clock window as the baseline below;
- if neither gap produced a trigger, conclude **inconclusive** (say so explicitly) and re-check at the next gap or at the next usage-limit/quota block rather than recording a fake pass.

## Baseline (pre-fix)

Recorded evidence, for the record:

- 2026-11-03 **08:41:42** — every remote provider deterministically skipped (`munitoai-free` `usage_limit_reset_pending` reset ~15.4 h away; `opencode-go-3` `quota_exhausted` ~14 days; four entries `outside_available_window`) and the proxy logged `Chain exhausted ... holding 300s before restarting cycle` **three times**. The audit subprocess (`audit-RISE-0MVZEOVQG0075XSU-...`) received a 429 in 0.4 s and could never succeed; its 1080 s per-call screen budget was consumed by holds.
- 2026-11-03 **08:40:05** — `Returning first provider error response instead of generic exhausted message ... (status=400)` followed immediately by two 300 s holds (the first provider's raw 400 carried no `Retry-After`, which is what re-enabled the "legacy full hold").
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:40** — local guard refused with `eta_prefill_s=45.2 enforced=true` and the request was routed onto the dead remote chain (`outcome=exhausted`); **08:50:41** the identical prompt and identical ETA were admitted (`enforced=false`, `eta_occupancy_s=0.0`) and produced a first byte in 6 s.
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:31.690** — `local_dispatch_denied session=... owner=... active=1` on a two-slot pool while `/llama/local/status` at 08:49:31.034 reported `available_slots=2`: the refusal named an owner and a count but not which gate refused.

### Measured baseline — log file `proxy.log.2026-11-03_101625`, window 08:37:26 → 10:16:25 UTC (99 min)

This is the pre-fix window captured by the log rotated at the 10:16 restart. It sits inside the `06:00–10:00` closed gap, i.e. it is the like-for-like comparison window.

| Signal | Count (99 min) |
|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted for model=` (holds taken) | **105** — 36 of them `holding 300s`, plus 30 s / 120 s / 38 s / 17 s variants |
| `All providers exhausted for model=` | 189 |
| deterministic-skip vocabulary | `usage_limit_reset_pending` 1198 · `outside its available_times window` 884 · `quota_exhausted` 1230 |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` | 137 |
| … of which `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` | **57** (11 distinct sessions) |
| `local_dispatch_denied` | 26 (none carrying occupancy evidence) |

### Control window — open windows, no trigger expected

`proxy.log`, 10:16:29 → 13:34:50 UTC (3 h 18 m; remote windows **open** that whole time): `Chain exhausted` **0**, `All providers exhausted` **0**, `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` 334 (46 × `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` — correct fall-throughs, because remote had capacity), `local_dispatch_denied` 97. Use this as the "no trigger + open chain" reference: it shows what a *healthy* zero looks like, and it is why "0 holds" alone proves nothing.

Log retention is 7 days (`Pruned old rotated log ... > 7 days old`), so the baseline file survives until ~2026-11-10. Re-extract the numbers above if it is needed after that; do not assume it is still there.

## Measurement technique

Rules that keep the comparison honest:

1. **Like-for-like windows only.** Compare post-fix samples taken inside a *closed* window (`01:00–04:00` / `06:00–10:00` UTC) against the baseline above. Never compare an open-window sample against it; an open chain cannot trigger the fix, so it will always look "fixed".
2. **Normalise per hour** — sample lengths will differ; report counts per hour as well as raw counts.
3. **Check chain aliveness before interpreting a zero.** If no trigger fired, prove the chain was actually provably dead in that window (`munitoai-free` unavailable *and* the four window-gated providers closed). A zero with a live chain is `inconclusive`, not `fixed`.
4. **Exclude the restart verification probe** from the sample: session `verify-lp-0mw0kzr7a003ufqk-restart` (2026-11-03 14:25:54, 18/8/26 tokens) exists only to prove the deploy.
5. **Quote the log line, not the count**, for anything that decides the verdict — a count can be satisfied by a wrong reason.

### LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (fail fast / no bounce) — expected post-fix signatures

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log            # or the rotated file covering the chosen window
# 1. the fail-fast line replaces the hold, on one vocabulary
grep -c 'chain_planned_unavailable'          $LOG    # expect > 0 in a provably-dead window
grep -m3 'chain_planned_unavailable'         $LOG    # inspect reason=, hold=skipped, retry_after=, deterministic_skips=, terminal=
# 2. no hold on a provably dead chain
grep -c 'Chain exhausted for model='         $LOG    # expect 0 in that window (baseline: 105/99 min)
# 3. the local override instead of a bounce onto a dead chain
grep -c 'local_admission_guard_local_wait'   $LOG    # expect > 0 where the old code emitted direct_fallback
grep 'local_admission_guard_direct_fallback' $LOG | grep -c 'reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct'   # expect 0 *while the chain is dead* (baseline 57)
# 4. retry timing is honest (earliest reset, body == header, capped)
grep 'chain_planned_unavailable' $LOG | grep -o 'retry_after=[0-9]*' | sort -u
# 5. the client-visible shape (the preserved first error, now timed)
grep 'Returning first provider error response' $LOG | tail -3
# 6. the report renders the new section
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24   # "## Chain-end outcomes"
```

Targets:

| Metric | Baseline | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted` (holds) per closed-window hour | 105 / 1.65 h ≈ **64/h** | **0** where every skip is deterministic; unchanged for transient chains (cooldown / 5xx / connection error) — verify at least one transient hold still occurs |
| `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped` | 0 (line did not exist) | > 0, one per affected request (not per provider) |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` with a dead chain | 57 / 99 min | **0**, replaced by `local_admission_guard_local_wait` |
| `All providers exhausted` reached from a local ETA refusal | the 08:49:40 shape | **0** |
| audit-* call latency on a doomed chain | 300 s × 3 holds before the error | < 1 s |
| Advertised `retry_after` | cap-derived (3600) or absent | the earliest known reset, capped by `max_retry_after_seconds`, equal to the `Retry-After` header |

Per-line acceptance (AC2/AC4 of the item):
- `local_admission_guard_local_wait` must appear **with** `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` and **without** a following `→ routing to next provider` line;
- `chain_planned_unavailable` must **not** appear in a window where a provider was merely cooling down (that would be a false positive — the verdict must stay conservative).

### LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 (diagnostics) — this half is measurable within hours

Denials happen under local contention (26 in 99 min pre-fix; 97 in 3 h 18 m), so this verdict does not need a closed window:

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
# every denial must carry the evidence suffix (fields: records_total, records_active,
# records_unexpired, records_stale, active_counter, max_local, generating,
# prefill_in_flight, prefill_cap, llama_available_slots, llama_total_slots, records=…)
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied'                                  $LOG
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied.*records_total='                  $LOG    # expect == the count above
# contradictions are logged, and the "our own numbers cannot explain it" class must be zero
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=llama_reports_free_slots'  $LOG   # > 0 is fine (prefill cap vs llama view)
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=occupancy_unexplained'     $LOG   # must be 0 — non-zero is a bookkeeping defect, file it
# which cap refused is now readable without a repro
grep -m3 'local_dispatch_denied' $LOG | grep -o 'generating=[0-9]*\|prefill_in_flight=[0-9]*\|prefill_cap=[0-9]*\|max_local=[0-9]*'
```

Targets: 100 % of `local_dispatch_denied` lines carry the evidence; `occupancy_unexplained` **0**; the 08:49:31 question ("denied with `available_slots=2` — which gate?") answerable from the line alone (expect `prefill_in_flight=1 prefill_cap=1`, i.e. the serialised-prefill cap, for that shape).

## Decision criteria

| Outcome | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **fixed** | a provably-dead window shows ≥1 `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped`, **0** holds, and the evidence suffix on every denial | close with the numbers; no follow-up |
| **partial** | fail-fast fires but a hold still occurs on a deterministic chain, or a denial lacks the evidence suffix | file a `test-failure`/bug item naming the exact line and reason; do not close |
| **not fixed** | a provably-dead window still shows `Chain exhausted` / `direct_fallback`, and no `chain_planned_unavailable` | reopen LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (or file a new bug) with the window and the log lines |
| **inconclusive** | no provably-dead window occurred in the sample | record it, keep the item open, re-check at the next gap/usage-limit block; never record a pass |
| **regression** | holds disappear on *transient* chains too (cooldown/5xx), or `occupancy_unexplained` > 0 | treat as a defect: the verdict is over-firing |

If any outcome requires code change, create the follow-up item (`discovered-from:<this id>`) and implement it in its own worktree — this item is measurement only.

## Out of scope

- Changing provider `available_times` or adding an always-on remote provider (the operator rejected that on 2026-10-31; see LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN).
- Extending the classifier or the `chain_planned_unavailable` vocabulary — that is now owned by epic LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN (its AC11, extend-never-fork).
- Re-litigating the incident's per-call budget arithmetic.

## Candidate follow-up observed during the restart (not measured here)

Before the 2026-11-03 14:25 restart, `/llama/local/status` reported `llama_server_running=true`, `available_slots=2/2`, `capacity_hint=idle` for ~3 hours while **no `llama-server` process existed** (`llama-server.log` ends `start-llama.sh: line 273: 4168 Killed` at 11:33) and local dispatches were failing with `ConnectError`. `/health` said `healthy` throughout. That is a stale *running-state* divergence (distinct from the slot-count divergence fixed in LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5): file it separately with this evidence if it reproduces — it is a candidate for the same "engine view vs route view" family.

## Assumptions

- The deployed code is what runs: proxy started 14:25:09 UTC, `dev` HEAD `7892d22d` committed 12:54 — confirm again at evaluation time with `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>` and `git log -1 --format=%cI dev`.
- `munitoai-free` remains the only unrestricted remote, so every provably-dead window is of the shape above; if a provider is added or re-timed, re-derive the window table before comparing.
- The 7-day log retention is long enough to reach the earliest evaluation date; if it is not, the baseline numbers in this description are the record.

## Scheduling hold (do NOT implement before the gate instant)

The title carries the earliest instant, but a title cannot stop `wl next` from
dispatching this item tonight, which would produce a premature sample. The item
is therefore parked with a **descriptive timer hold** as its assignee:
`not-before-2026-11-04T04:00Z` (a non-empty assignee is a scheduling hold, so
`wl next` skips it). This is a timer label, not an agent claim — no agent owns
this item.

At or after **2026-11-04 04:00 UTC**, release it and implement:

```bash
wl update LP-0MW0S88WJ005SBPH --assignee "" --json    # release the timer hold
wl show LP-0MW0S88WJ005SBPH --json                    # then /skill:implement <id>
```

If you are reading this *before* the gate instant because someone released the
hold early, do not measure: say so, re-apply the hold, and wait for the first
complete closed window. If the 01:00–04:00 gap on 2026-11-04 turns out to have a
live `munitoai-free`, the preferred sample is the 06:00–10:00 gap, evaluated at
2026-11-04 10:00 UTC.
data.title: Evaluate the chain fail-fast and lease-diagnostics outcome (earliest 2026-11-05 15:35 UTC)

data.description:
## Goal

**As an** operator, **I want** the local dispatch counters to return to zero on their own after every completed request, **so that** the self-healing recovery loop is a safety net rather than the normal path — a counter that only clears via `counter recovered: reset from N to 0` means the decrement path that should have cleared it did not run.

## Evidence (measured 2026-11-03, 14:25:10 → 15:01 UTC, proxy pid 158427, `dev` `7892d22d`)

30 minutes of an agent-fleet burst (808 streams, 26.6 req/min, peak 71/min) produced **24 counter-recovery events in 36 minutes**, with no client-visible failure:

```
  9  local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 2 to 1 (1 active dispatch records)
  8  local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0 (0 active dispatch records)
  8  active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0 (no active dispatch records or local queries in flight)
  4  local_generating_queries counter recovered: reclaimed 1 stale session(s) (reset from 1 to 0, 1 sessions removed from local_generating_sessions)
```

Shape of the drift:

- the counter is **higher than the authoritative record set** in every case (`from 2` with `1 active dispatch record`, `from 1` with `0`), i.e. an increment whose matching decrement never landed;
- the recovery runs later than the offending request: recoveries cluster in the *low*-rate minutes (14:46: 7 streams / 5 recoveries; 14:48: 34 / 8) and are absent from the two rate peaks (14:28: 64 streams, 14:37: 71 streams, 0 recoveries) — so the leak is masked while load is continuous and surfaces when traffic thins out;
- `local_generating_sessions` accumulated a stale member (`reclaimed 1 stale session(s)`), which is the set the generating-only pool sizes itself from.

Consequence if it drifts the other way (counter too *high*): the 03:00 behaviour family is a false 503 for every other session — `local_concurrency_limit` is already the second-largest local-refusal reason in this window (63 of 657 refusals), so a counter that reads high is not cosmetic.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than watching

The recovery loop (`_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` / `_recover_stuck_global_active_queries` / the generating-only reclaim) logs at WARNING, so this is 24 WARNING-level signals of a decrement path that is not airtight, on a workload the proxy is expected to serve. The row `reset from 2 to 1 (1 active dispatch records)` is the clearest: one record exists, two counted — exactly one decrement lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A completed local stream (success, client disconnect, deadline cancel, and error) always leaves `local_active_queries`, `active_queries`, `local_generating_queries` and `local_generating_sessions` at their pre-request value — asserted per exit path, with the record set and the counter compared.
- AC2: A concentrated burst test (N concurrent local dispatches, mixed completion/disconnect/cancel) ends with every counter at 0 and no `counter recovered` line — the recovery loop must not fire in a healthy run.
- AC3: Identify **which** exit path loses the decrement (the counters are incremented in different places — `_increment_local_active_queries` / `_increment_active_queries` / `_increment_generating_only_slot` — so the fix names the missing counterpart rather than adding another reconciliation).
- AC4: The recovery loop keeps working as the safety net (it must not be removed), and its WARNING stays visible.
- AC5: Regression test that reproduces the lost decrement deterministically (not by timing) and passes only when AC1 holds.

## Out of scope

- Rewriting the dispatch-lease model itself (LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 covered the stale-record and diagnostics half).
- The `local_generating_sessions` reclamation TTL tuning unless AC3 shows it is the leak.

## Key files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_increment_local_active_queries`, `_decrement_local_active_queries`, `_increment_local_generating_sessions`, `_increment_generating_only_slot`, `_decrement_generating_only_slot`, `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries`, `_recover_stuck_global_active_queries`, `_get_generating_only_count`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — the dispatch/complete/cancel exit paths around `proxy_to_local`.
- `proxy/tests/` — an extension of `test_recover_stuck_global_active_queries.py` plus a new burst/counter-invariant suite.

## Assumptions

- No client-visible failure accompanied the drift in this window (0 stalls, 0 re-routes, 0 5xx), so this is a latent correctness/observability defect rather than an active outage.
- The incidents that motivated the recovery loop (LP-0MTYAWDCQ006RGYU) are the reason it must stay.

## Provenance

## Goal

**As an** operator watching long local prefills, **I want** the proxy to actually observe per-slot prefill progress, **so that** a local dispatch lease is extended from measured progress instead of an estimate — because "no progress visible, trust the estimate" is precisely the combination behind the 4-hour wedged-lease incident (LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O).

## Evidence (measured 2026-11-03, 14:25:10 → 15:01 UTC, `dev` `7892d22d`)

13 `prefill_progress_unobservable` warnings during a burst of 87 local streams:

```
prefill_progress_unobservable: no per-slot or aggregate prefill progress;
lease extension relies on the adaptive acquisition estimate and liveness signal
```

In the same window, local first-byte latency on those dispatches:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` | n=85, p50 **3 750 ms**, p90 **28 651 ms**, max **71 128 ms** |
| `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold` at `waited=30s` | 15 |
| local `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=idle_timeout` | 1 (elapsed_s=40.1) |

Meanwhile llama-server *does* report progress — it logs `slot update_slots: id 0 | task 18016 | prompt processing progress, n_tokens = 23410 ...` throughout the same period — so the information exists at the backend and is not reaching the proxy's lease-extension path. That is the gap: the proxy falls back to its estimate while the truth is one `/slots` field away.

80–390 k-token prompts at ~3.9 ms/token mean a single prefill can legitimately run for minutes; an estimate-based lease extension on that duration is exactly the window in which a lease either expires mid-prefill (retry/cancel churn) or is held past a dead client (the wedge).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Identify why per-slot prefill progress is unavailable in this deployment (backend build not reporting `n_past` / `prompt_progress`, the proxy's `/slots` selector choosing the router port instead of the model child, or the aggregate fallback not reading the field that *is* present) and fix it so a local prefill in progress yields a measured progress signal.
- AC2: When a measured signal exists, the prefill lease extension uses it (progress advanced ⇒ extend; no progress ⇒ the no-progress watchdog's decision), and `prefill_progress_unobservable` is not logged for that dispatch.
- AC3: The unobservable case keeps today's fail-safe behaviour (estimate + liveness), still logs the WARNING, and is now counted/attributable so a persistent rate is visible rather than only in a log stream.
- AC4: A test with a stubbed `/slots` payload that carries progress asserts the measured path is taken; a payload without it asserts the fail-safe path plus the warning.
- AC5: Document the signal's provenance (which llama.cpp field, which endpoint, which fallback order) in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Out of scope

- Changing the prefill deadline / budget knobs (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`).
- The measured-cache-abort path (LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135).

## Key files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_extend_lease_during_prefill`, `_query_prefill_progress`, `_resolve_local_slots_target`, the `prefill_progress_unobservable` emitter.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `_query_slots` / `_query_slots_detail` and the per-slot `context_tokens` / `n_past` fields.
- `proxy/tests/` — `test_prefill_lease_extension.py`, `test_measured_prefill_regression.py`, `test_direct_slots_polling_fix.py`.

## Assumptions

- The llama.cpp build in use may genuinely not expose `n_past` (b8782 dropped it); if so, AC1's remedy is the aggregate or `context_tokens` route already used by the residency ladder (`measured_last_dispatch`), and AC5 documents that as the supported signal.
- A 71 s local first byte is acceptable *if* progress is observed and the client is alive; the defect is the blindness, not the duration.

## Provenance

## Goal

**As an** operator reading the after-acceptance eviction signal, **I want** a local dispatch that **completed successfully** to be released without being reported as `local_eviction_after_acceptance`, **so that** the AC7(a) defect detector (LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S) counts real evictions instead of ordinary lease expiry.

## Evidence (2026-11-03 14:25:54 → 14:26:34 UTC, `dev` `7892d22d`)

A small verification request that **succeeded in 0.57 s** was 40 s later reported as an eviction after acceptance:

```
14:25:54  routing_check provider=local-qwen3 ... estimated_tokens=8
14:25:54  [local] POST ...  Stream finished: reason=length tokens=18/8/26 stream=false
14:25:54  lease_renewed session=verify-... timeout=30s
14:25:54  local_preference_resolved preference=remote-ok outcome=local reason=none
14:26:34  local_eviction     ... reason=slot_assignment_freed slot=0
14:26:34  local_eviction_after_acceptance ... reason=idle_timeout estimated_tokens=8
          new_tokens=8 eta_prefill_s=0.0 elapsed_s=40.1
14:26:34  lease_released session=verify-... reason=idle_timeout
```

Three things are wrong together:

1. `local_eviction_after_acceptance` is documented as "accepted local dispatches evicted **before their first byte**" — this request produced its first byte (and its last) within 0.57 s, so it was never evicted *after acceptance* in the intended sense;
2. `elapsed_s=40.1` is the *lease's* idle lifetime (30 s timeout + slack), not the request duration — so the field mixes two different clocks;
3. the event is emitted on the routine `lease_released ... reason=idle_timeout` path, which is the normal way every completed local dispatch's record expires.

Measured frequency in this window: 7 `local_eviction` lines, 6 `reason=slot_assignment_freed` (expected churn) and 1 `reason=idle_timeout` — i.e. 100 % of the `idle_timeout` eviction reports in the sample are false positives, and the true-positive rate of the signal cannot be established while that is the case.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The `local_eviction_after_acceptance` event is emitted only when a dispatch was admitted and did **not** reach its first byte (the documented meaning); a completed or cancelled-after-first-byte dispatch releases silently or under its own reason.
- AC2: `elapsed_s` measures the request's own lifetime (admission → release), not the lease timeout, so the value agrees with the request's observed duration.
- AC3: A regression test drives the pattern above — one local dispatch that completes, then the idle lease release — and asserts **no** `local_eviction_after_acceptance` line; a second test drives a genuine admitted-then-never-first-byte dispatch and asserts the line **is** emitted with a truthful `elapsed_s`.
- AC4: Existing consumers keep working: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` stays a distinct event from `local_eviction`, its `reason` vocabulary is unchanged, and the usage-analysis report's after-acceptance breakdown (which splits by reason) still renders.
- AC5: Documentation of the event's meaning in `proxy/docs/routing.md` matches the behaviour.

## Out of scope

- The eviction reasons themselves (`measured_cache_deficit`, `prefill_deadline`, `idle_timeout`) and their thresholds.
- Any change to how leases are released — only to what is *reported* about the release.

## Key files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` — the `local_eviction` / `local_eviction_after_acceptance` emitters.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the idle-timeout / slot-assignment-free release paths and the dispatcher that records the event.
- `proxy/tests/` — `test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`, `test_lease_truthfulness.py`, and the usage-analysis `test_post_acceptance_eviction_report.py` contract.

## Assumptions

- The `slot_assignment_freed` line emitted immediately before it is the expected churn line and is not part of the defect.
- The window's single occurrence is representative of the routine path (every completed local dispatch leaves a record that later expires by `idle_timeout`), not a one-off; AC1/AC3 make that checkable rather than assumed.

## Provenance
